newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's economy seen growing 4 pct in 1997 - IBEF.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's economy seen growing 4 pct in 1997 - IBEF.

text.p: Brazil's economy is likely to grow 4.0 percent in 1997, with inflation reaching a maximum of 9.0 percent next year, the Brazilian Institute of Financial Executives (IBEF) said.

IBEF said in a report on economic forecasts for 1997 it expects the country's trade gap to remain steady at between 4.5 and 5.0 billion reais in 1997 and the public deficit to reach 3.0 percent of the country's gross domestic product next year. It also said real interest rates are likely to drop to between 10 and 15 percent a year and noted that foreign exchange policy should not suffer any changes.

Regarding foreign investment, IBEF said direct investment is likely to hit up to $10 billion in 1997. Corporate and consumer defaults are expected to remain high next year, reaching on average 10 percent of total bank loans, it said.

IBEF said unemployment is likely to increase in 1997 because Brazilian private companies will continue to adjust themselves to foreign competition. It also said the privatization of state firms and cuts in public spending are likely to force companies to lay off more workers.
